 Harris County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0017
 Randall Duncan, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Plaintiff's Original Petition
Filed:
December 11, 2024
Plaintiff's counsel:
Daniel Stein, Dunn & Acosta LLP
PARTIES
Plaintiff Randall Duncan is an individual residing in Texas who was the driver of a passenger vehicle involved in the collision
described below. The Defendant is an automobile insurance company authorized to write motor vehicle policies in the State of
Texas, which issued a policy of insurance that provided coverage to the Plaintiff at the time of the loss. Defendant may be served
through its registered agent in accordance with the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.
FACTS
On June 28, 2023, Plaintiff was lawfully operating his vehicle through a signalized intersection in Sugar Land when another
motor vehicle entered the intersection and struck the side of Plaintiff's car. The impact occurred with force sufficeint to push
Plaintiff's vehicle across the lane and deploy airbags. Plaintiff reported the collision to Defendant promptly and submitted the
information needed to evaluate his claim under the coverage in force. Defendant has not paid the benefits owed under the policy
in the amount Plaintiff is entitled to recover.
NEGLIGENCE
Defendant, through its insured or the responsible driver covered under the policy, failed to keep a proper lookout, failed to yield
the right of way, and operated its vehicle at a speed and in a manner that a reasonably prudent driver would not have used under
the same circumstances. Defendant further breached its contractual and statutory duties to investigate the claim in good faith, to
affirm or deny coverage within a reasonable time, and to pay covered amounts once liability became reasonably clear.
DAMAGES
As a direct result of the collision, Plaintiff suffered a fracture of the wrist that required medical evaluation, immobilization, and
ongoing treatment. Plaintiff has incurred medical expenses, lost wages, and loss of use of his hand, and he continues to
experience pain and reduced function. Plaintiff seeks recovery of actual damages, pre-judgment and post-judgment interest,
statutory damages available under the Texas Insurance Code, and court costs. Plaintiff therefore requests judgment against
Defendant in the amount of $126,000.00.
